newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares seen steady to lower.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares seen steady to lower.

text.p: 0800 GMT - Hungarian share prices were seen moving sideways or dropping slightly on Friday on a market waiting for Q1 corporate results and a global offering of oil and gas company MOL, traders said.
* Plastic maker Pannonplast, which published its Q1 earnings report earlier on Friday, was seen rising.
* MOL was expected to remain around Thursday's price levels.

Hungarian shares were seen moving sideways or drift slightly lower on Friday in a quiet market waiting for 1997 first quarter earnings reports and an offering of oil and gas company MOL, traders said.
"I expect a day similar to yesterday," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities. "Turnover will be probably relatively low...and some papers may ease."
On Thursday, the BUX index finished at 5,789.04 points, down 51.61.
Traders said most shares were likely to stagnate or even drop.
"Everybody is waiting for the Q1 results and the MOL offering," a trader said.
First quarter corporate results will be published in the first half of May.

A global offering of at least 12.5 percent in MOL will be priced on May 6, and traders said the market was waiting for the price of the shares, which is likely to be at a discount compared with the price on the Budapest Stock Exchange.
MOL closed at 3,215 forints on Thursday.
Traders said there would be substantial demand for MOL at slightly lower price levels but the share was not likely to move much on Friday.
However, if buying interest from foreigners emerged, it could propel MOL and prevent a fall in the BUX index, traders said.
